review.title: A CI step that hangs reports 'in progress' for six hours instead of failing
review.acceptance:
REQUIRED: the jobs in ci.yml and windows.yml get `timeout-minutes`, per step where a step has a credible hang and per job otherwise. THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. PL-0735 fixes the one step that hangs today; this makes the NEXT one visible. A step with no bound burns GitHub's six-hour default and reports 'in progress' the entire time -- indistinguishable, to the only readable channel this project has (annotations, because job logs need a login), from a runner that is merely queued. That is how CI #181 and #182 both sat unfinished without anyone treating it as a failure.

REQUIRED: each bound is derived from an OBSERVED duration and the derivation is written beside it. A number somebody felt was generous is a number somebody will raise the first time it fires. Observed today: e2e 5m 8s, e2e-typecheck 12s, and the Windows e2e-desktop job 3m 25s.

REQUIRED: the bound is not so tight that a slow runner reads as a defect. A timeout that fires on a cold cache teaches people to re-run rather than to read, which costs more than the hang.

OUT OF SCOPE: the control-plane performance work, which is PL-0735, and any change to what the steps do.
review.notes:
SPLIT OUT OF PL-0735 in round 112, carrying its clause verbatim. PL-0735 was filed holding ci.yml and `ai:claim` refused it on an overlap with PL-0728, which is in REVIEW for the rest of the round. Keeping both halves in one task meant neither landed; this one is BACKLOG until ci.yml frees.

Classification C (workflow/harness defect) under the round-112 directive's A-E scheme, same as PL-0735. P1 rather than P0 because PL-0735 removes the hang that exists; this prevents the one that does not exist yet.

review.title: A task parked for an external reviewer consumes local implementation capacity
review.acceptance:
claude-infra's maxParallel has gone 1 -> 2 (round 109) -> 3 (round 113) -> 4 -> 5 (round 114). Every raise was justified against the same three documented conditions and every one of them held. That is the symptom, not the cause.

THE CAUSE: usageByAgent counts REVIEW toward maxParallel, and REVIEW here usually means 'parked for gpt-architect', who is not a locally executable agent. So a lane whose entire output is awaiting an EXTERNAL verdict consumes its own implementation capacity, and the only lever available is a number that was never meant to be pulled five times.

REQUIRED: a task in REVIEW whose reviewAgent is not locally executable does not count toward its owner's maxParallel. It still holds its allowedPaths -- CONFLICT DETECTION MUST NOT CHANGE, and that is the whole safety argument for the capacity limit being loosenable at all: overlap is prevented structurally by allowedPaths regardless of owner or count.
REQUIRED: 'locally executable' is read from the registry, not hard-coded to gpt-architect.
REQUIRED: a task in REVIEW with a LOCAL reviewAgent still counts, because that reviewer is real work this organisation has to do.
REQUIRED: the capacity raises this defect forced are reconsidered once it lands. If the right number for claude-infra is 2, it should go back to 2.
REQUIRED: driven by a scenario over FIXTURES, not the live board, per this suite's own standing rule, and shown to fail before the change.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing activeStatuses, which conflict detection reads. Only the capacity computation moves.
review.notes: FILED ROUND 114 during the release sprint, at the moment a fifth raise became the alternative to leaving PL-0734 -- item 2 on the release-impact list, directly on the launch path -- unstarted. Filed rather than fixed on the spot because scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs is reserved by PL-0735 in review, and because a control-plane change made in a hurry during a release sprint is how a scheduler quietly starts producing different waves.

unit.evidence:
node scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs: 72 scenarios, all pass, 133.9s. repo:validate passed. ai:validate: 150 tasks, 9 agents, no errors.

SHOWN TO FAIL BEFORE THE CHANGE, as the acceptance requires and not merely asserted. With scenario 10u in place and scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs stashed back to its pre-change state, the suite stopped at:

  [ 148.6s] 10u. A lane parked for an EXTERNAL reviewer does not spend its own capacity
  AI control plane error: claude-lead is at maxParallel 2

That message IS the defect: claude-lead held two tasks in REVIEW for gpt-architect -- an agent this repository cannot run -- and could not claim a third with entirely disjoint paths. The implementation was then restored and the file compared byte-for-byte against the copy taken before stashing.

OVER FROZEN FIXTURES, never the live board, per this suite's standing rule. claude-lead's real maxParallel is 2 today and borrowing it would make the scenario a bet on that staying true.

FOUR CASES, and the three that are not the headline are the ones that keep this safe:
  1. two REVIEWs for gpt-architect (external) + one READY -> the claim now succeeds.
  2. two REVIEWs for claude-test (LOCAL) + one READY -> still refused at maxParallel 2. That review is work this organisation owes; the slot is honest.
  3. two REVIEWs naming "gpt-architekt", which is in no registry -> still refused. A typo in a field must not silently buy capacity, and this is the direction of error that is cheap to write and expensive to find.
  4. a REVIEW parked externally whose paths overlap a READY candidate -> STILL REFUSED, with "PL-CAP-0032 paths overlap active task PL-CAP-0031 owned by claude-lead".

Case 4 is the whole safety argument. conflictWithActive still reads active(), untouched, so a task in REVIEW keeps its allowedPaths reserved exactly as before; activeStatuses is unchanged. Overlap is prevented structurally by declared paths regardless of owner or count, which is precisely why capacity can be relaxed without two agents ever writing the same file. Re-proved against the LIVE board as well: PL-0738 and PL-0730 are both still refused on their real overlap with PL-0736.

LOCAL EXECUTABILITY IS READ FROM THE REGISTRY, not hard-coded: consumesCapacity asks agentExecutable(reviewer, d), the same question dispatch already asks, which resolves through the adapter serving that agent's kind.

TWO NUMBERS WHERE THERE WAS ONE, because they are now two facts. The status report would otherwise have shown capacity falling with no explanation of where the work went. It now reads, against the live board: "claude-infra: 0/5 capacity in use, 3 active (3 parked for an external reviewer)" -- which is the five-raise situation, stated.

FOUND WHILE DOING THIS, recorded as its own defect.found: the suite's summary line carried a hand-typed "(73 scenarios)" and was wrong by two -- 71 call sites existed, 72 now. A false number inside a PASSING suite's own report. The count is derived in scenario() now and cannot drift.

NOT DONE, AND SPLIT OUT AS PL-0747: the acceptance's final clause, reconsidering the raises. control/agents.json is in this task's reviewDependencies and not its allowedPaths, so this task cannot write it -- and the clause itself says "once it lands", which has not happened. Judging whether 2 is right for claude-infra needs the board observed under the new accounting, and lowering numbers in the same commit that changes how they are counted would put two decisions under one review.

review.title: The commander's qualification evidence is collected by hand, one command at a time
review.acceptance:
PW-0504 is the OBSERVATION and stays blocked on hardware. This is the PREPARATION, which is engineering, and gpt-architect's round-115 section 4 asks for it by name: 'First prepare the smallest deterministic qualification package/checklist... Prepare this so Diego's part is minimal.'

TODAY THE RUN SHEET ASKS THE COMMANDER TO TYPE POWERSHELL AND PASTE OUTPUT. Step 0 alone is three separate snippets plus two settings pages read by eye, and every later row asks him to notice and copy something. Each hand-copied field is a field that can be wrong, missing, or from the wrong machine, and 'a RIG pass on unrecorded hardware is not evidence' is this document's own rule.

REQUIRED: one command Diego runs AFTER installing and launching, which collects everything collectable without him transcribing anything -- the environment block the matrix specifies (Windows build, GPU and driver, WebView2 runtime, display, audio), the installed tree's location and whether verify-install accepts it, whether sidecar.log exists with its size and tail, whether a liberty-desktop.exe process and its node.exe child are running, and whether the handshake line is present in the log.
REQUIRED: it writes ONE file he sends back, and prints a short human summary so he can see whether it worked before sending it.
REQUIRED: ABSENCE IS RECORDED, NOT SKIPPED. A missing sidecar.log, an unresolvable WebView2 version or a process that is not running are findings the report must state explicitly -- the run sheet already says an absent log is itself a finding, and a collector that silently omitted it would undo that.
REQUIRED: IT CLAIMS NOTHING IT CANNOT SEE. It must not report that WebView2 rendered the application, that playback worked, or that the window appeared. Those are the commander's eyes and the report must say so where it would otherwise be read as covering them. gpt's round-105 section 9: do not collapse those claims.
REQUIRED: NO SECRETS. It must not capture the launch token, environment dumps, or anything from the handshake line beyond host and port.
REQUIRED: testable off Windows. Every platform fact arrives through an injected reader, the way installed-identity.mjs takes `env` as a parameter, so the composition and the absence-handling have a suite on this machine. The Windows commands themselves cannot be executed here and that limit is stated rather than glossed.
REQUIRED: the run sheet's Step 0 and its report format point at the command instead of listing snippets to retype, and the rows only a person can judge stay a person's.

OUT OF SCOPE: marking any PW-0504 row passed. This task delivers the collector; the evidence is still the commander's to produce.
review.notes:
FILED ROUND 115 under gpt-architect's instruction to minimise the commander's work before asking for it. The one-command shape is chosen because the alternative already exists and is the problem: the run sheet is correct and it is long, and length is what makes a qualification session get abbreviated.

Scope held deliberately narrow. This does not automate judgement -- G1's compositing result, G2's scaling, the SmartScreen wording, whether a window actually appeared -- only the facts a machine can read about itself.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs: 18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail. node --check clean. repo:validate passed. node --test scripts/assert-no-row-runs-nowhere.test.mjs: 14/14, unaffected.

THE FIX, AND IT IS NOT A REDACTOR. gpt-architect's finding was correct: sidecarLog returned tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES), which put whatever happened to be in the log -- a token in a URL, an argv, an environment dump -- into a file written to be pasted into a chat. The tail is GONE. In its place, classifyLog() reads the same 16 KiB window and reports ONLY which entries of a fixed signature table matched, plus line and byte counts.

AN ALLOWLIST, NOT A DENYLIST, and that choice is the substance of the fix. Redacting things that "look like secrets" cannot work, because a secret is whatever happened to be in that file and no pattern enumerates it. So nothing the log said can reach the report: the report can only say which of ten patterns written in this repository matched, which is a fact about the table rather than about the file. Each pattern carries a plain-English `means` written here for a reader who has the report and not the machine -- which is the diagnostic value the raw tail had, minus the bytes. The ten: port-in-use, address-unavailable, permission-denied, file-missing, module-missing, module-format, native-module-failed, node-not-found, unhandled-error, fatal.

THE DANGEROUS FAILURE MODE OF AN ALLOWLIST IS HANDLED AND TESTED. A real error nobody wrote a signature for returns an empty list, which reads like "no problem". The note distinguishes them in those words -- "NO RECOGNISED FAILURE SIGNATURE in the examined window. That is not the same as 'no error'" -- it names the file to edit, and it points at the log on the machine, so nothing diagnostic is lost; it just does not travel unless the commander chooses to send it.

THE TEST THE REVIEWER ASKED FOR, AND WHY TWO TESTS THAT EACH LOOKED RIGHT LEFT THE LEAK UNCOVERED. There were already two: one asserted the fixture secret was absent from JSON.stringify(log.handshake) -- one subtree of the returned object -- and one asserted the WHOLE report was clean but fed sidecarLog a CLEAN log fixture. Between them, neither could ever have seen the tail. Now: the fixture hides the same string in THREE places, including an argv line and a URL inside an error line that the handshake logic never looks at; the sidecarLog test asserts on JSON.stringify(log) entire; and the existing full-report test was STRENGTHENED to use that adversarial fixture rather than a second near-duplicate test being added beside it. Both also assert that no raw log line, no URL from the log and no "[out]" prefix reaches the report, and the human-readable summarise() output is checked too, because that is what actually gets pasted.

SIX MUTANTS, ALL CAUGHT: (1) restoring tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES); (2) adding a "harmless" lastLine field; (3) having the classifier quote the line it matched; (4) deleting the module-format signature from the table; (5) softening the no-signature note to "Nothing to report."; (6) making the examined window unbounded. All six reverted, 18/18 green afterwards. Mutant 4 is caught by a new test that drives one sample line through every pattern in the table, because a table nobody checks grows a dead entry.

docs/WINDOWS_CERTIFICATION.md no longer tells the commander the report carries the log's tail, states that it never quotes sidecar.log, and says why an allowlist rather than a redactor.

A SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST, REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED, AND IT IS ARGUABLY THE WORSE OF THE TWO: scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs RUNS NOWHERE. It is not in package.json's test:scripts, and no workflow invokes it -- grep across package.json and .github/workflows finds only test-lifecycle.mjs under scripts/windows. So this task's `unit` gate is a suite that executes only when someone types the command by hand, and the leak was caught by a human reading the code rather than by the suite, which would not have run in any case. I have NOT fixed it: package.json and the workflows are outside this task's allowedPaths, and widening a reviewed surface mid-cycle is the thing the path lock exists to prevent. PL-0730 -- "test:scripts and the CI validate job can disagree in one direction without anything noticing" -- is where it belongs, and it is currently deferred behind PL-0736. Flagging it in the handoff.

STATED, NOT GLOSSED, and unchanged from round 1: none of the PowerShell in qualify.mjs has been executed. Every reading is a Windows fact and this container is Linux. What is proven here is the composition, the absence-handling, the bounding and now the sanitisation, all through injected readers.

OUT OF SCOPE AND NOT DONE: no PW-0504 row is marked passed, and no Windows runtime pass is claimed -- the reviewer's instruction and the position this task has held since round 1. This delivers the collector; the evidence is still the commander's to produce.

THE FINDING: PL-0741's Windows qualification collector emits an unsanitized raw sidecar.log tail despite its NO SECRETS acceptance. sidecarLog() returns tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES); the fixture embeds secretish:'must-not-appear' in the handshake yet checks only JSON.stringify(log.handshake), not JSON.stringify(log) or the full report. review.title: A pasted addon manifest URL has no safe path into the adapter
review.acceptance:
FILED UNDER gpt-architect's ROUND-115 SECTION 6, WHICH BEGINS BY FORBIDDING THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION: "A repository audit found that Liberty ALREADY contains a substantial Stremio stream adapter under packages/provider-sdk/src/stremio/. DO NOT BUILD ANOTHER STREMIO CLIENT." This is a thin path ONTO that adapter and adds no protocol code, no second transport and no second rights model.

WHAT IS MISSING TODAY. Every piece of the flow exists except the first step and the shape that carries it. `checkUrl` validates, `fetchJson` resolves-and-pins and fetches, `parseStremioManifest` parses, `defineStremioSource` gates rights. Nothing accepts a `stremio://` URL -- the scheme has zero occurrences in the repository -- and nothing produces an object a UI can show a human BEFORE a source exists.

REQUIRED: `stremio://` is normalised to `https://` BEFORE the URL and network policy run, never after. A policy that runs on a scheme it does not recognise rejects a legitimate paste; a policy that runs after an unvalidated rewrite is a policy that judged a different URL than the one fetched. The normalisation is a scheme swap and nothing else -- it must not rewrite a host, a port or a path, and `stremio://` pointing at a loopback or private host is subject to exactly the same refusals as `https://` pointing there.

REQUIRED: the fetch goes through the EXISTING pinned transport in http.ts. Add-by-URL is precisely the transition url-policy.ts names -- "the moment this becomes the general server-side client for arbitrary operator- or user-configured addons, host-string checks are no longer a control at all" -- and the reason this task is safe to write is that PL-0710 already landed resolve-and-pin. No code path here may reach the network any other way.

REQUIRED: the result is a PREVIEW, and the type must make it impossible to mistake for an authorization. Name, version and declared resources, taken from the parsed manifest. It carries no `ContentRights`, is not branded `RIGHTS_DECLARED`, and cannot be handed to `createStremioProvider`. Section 7 of the directive is the invariant: "Stremio protocol compatibility is NOT playback authorization. A pasted URL must NEVER automatically become an authorized production source."

REQUIRED: becoming a source remains `defineStremioSource`, unchanged, with an explicit operator `rights` and `rightsBasis`. The preview feeds the form; it does not substitute for it, and nothing in it may be defaulted into a rights basis.

REQUIRED: every refusal is a typed reason, never a throw, matching the convention the rest of this directory already holds.

OUT OF SCOPE, and deliberately so: the settings UI, any API route, any persistence of user-added sources, and profile/repository scoping for them. Those are PL-0744 and they carry questions this task must not answer by accident -- whose rights declaration a user-added source carries, and whether a non-operator may add one at all.
review.notes: SPLIT FROM THE DIRECTIVE'S PRIORITY 5 ON PURPOSE. The directive describes the whole flow ADD-ONS -> ADD BY URL -> paste -> validate -> preview -> rights declaration -> save/enable. The SDK half is thin, reuses the existing adapter entirely and is the piece every possible UI shape needs. The UI half is a settings surface, an API route, a schema change and a rights-ownership question, which is not thin, is not release-critical for the primary journey, and would pull a security and rights review into a release sprint in order to ship a feature nobody has asked to use yet.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck in packages/provider-sdk (tsc --noEmit): clean. Caught a real defect first -- one normalizeAddonUrl call site still passed a single argument after the signature took the UrlPolicyOptions, TS2554 at add-by-url.test.ts:118. Repository-wide npm run lint: 12/12 tasks successful, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unused-import warnings in apps/web, untouched by this task).

unit.evidence:
npx vitest run in packages/provider-sdk: 13 files, 310 tests, all pass. add-by-url.test.ts contributes 22, and they were MUTATION-TESTED rather than merely observed green:

(1) MUTANT 'the convenience hole' -- make a stremio:// paste skip checkUrl (if (!checked.ok && !normalizedFromStremioScheme)). FIVE tests fail, including every identity case that runs the same host through both spellings and requires the outcomes to match. This is the defect the feature could most plausibly have shipped with.
(2) MUTANT 'unanchored regex' -- /stremio:\/\//i instead of /^stremio:\/\//i, so a stremio:// inside a query parameter gets rewritten. 1 test fails.
(3) MUTANT 'weakened note' -- replace the authorizationNote text with 'ok to use'. 1 test fails.

Under mutant (1) the rebinding case still PASSED, correctly: that defence lives in http.ts and the mutant did not touch it. The layering is asserted, not assumed.

NOT CLAIMED: no test here opens a real socket. resolve-and-pin.test.ts and pinned-transport.test.ts own that, and this file reuses their rig shape so that only the resolver and the transport port are doubles -- every refusal observed is produced by the production checkUrl / authoriseResolvedTarget path.

review.title: Every msiexec call in the lifecycle harness can wait forever
review.acceptance:
FOUND BY PL-0736 WHILE BOUNDING THE STEP THAT CONTAINS IT. `lifecycle.mjs` calls `spawnSync("msiexec.exe", args, { encoding: "utf8", windowsHide: true })` four times -- install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall -- and passes no `timeout`. Windows Installer serialises on the `_MSIExecute` mutex and a holder makes the next invocation WAIT rather than fail, so there is no deadline anywhere in the chain that decides F1, F3 and F4.

PL-0736 put a 15-minute `timeout-minutes` on the step. That is an OUTER bound and deliberately not the fix: when it fires, the whole step dies and the report says nothing about which case stalled or why.

REQUIRED: a `timeout` on each msiexec invocation, and a timed-out case REPORTED as a case outcome with its own reason, not collapsed into a crash. The harness already distinguishes exit 1 (a real case failure) from exit 2 (a refusal over arguments or platform) precisely so a configuration mistake is not filed as a product defect; a stall is a third thing and must not be filed as either.

REQUIRED: the bound is per-invocation and derived. A silent install of this MSI is seconds of work.

REQUIRED: a timed-out case is NEVER recorded as pass, and never as not-run with a reason that reads like a deliberate skip -- F2's `not-run` means 'the evidence does not exist', and a stall means 'we did not find out'.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what any case does, and the step-level bound PL-0736 added, which stays as the outer limit.
review.notes: P2 rather than P1 because the outer bound now exists, so the failure mode is 'the step dies at 15 minutes with a poor message' rather than 'the job burns an hour'. It is still a real defect: the message is what a person reads at 2am.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs: 42 tests, 42 pass (was 33; this task adds 9). Full npm run test:scripts: green, rc=0. repo:validate: passed.

TWO CASES RUN A REAL CHILD RATHER THAN ASSERTING A BELIEF ABOUT spawnSync. The whole repair rests on Node's timeout semantics, so they are exercised: a child that sleeps 60s with timeout 250 returns status null and error.code ETIMEDOUT; a missing binary returns status null and error.code ENOENT. THAT PAIR IS THE DEFECT -- the old code tested status !== 0, so a stall and an absent msiexec.exe both arrived as a bare fail with status: null and nothing to read.

MUTATION-TESTED, five ways this repair could be undone:
  no-timeout        (delete timeout from the spawn options)   -> 1 test fails
  stall-is-notrun   (a stall recorded as not-run)             -> 2 tests fail
  gate-off          (jobFailed returns false)                 -> 2 tests fail
  spawn-as-stall    (a spawn failure dressed as a timeout)    -> 1 test fails
  timeout-too-long  (180s -> 300s)                            -> 1 test fails

The first and last are the ones worth naming. no-timeout is the mutant every other case in this block would survive, because they drive classifyInvocation with synthetic results and would keep passing while timedOut quietly never became true again on a machine nobody in this container can run; it is caught only because the spawn options are a frozen exported value with an assertion on them. timeout-too-long is caught because the step bound arithmetic is ASSERTED rather than left in a comment: four invocations at 300s is 20 minutes against PL-0736's 15-minute timeout-minutes, so the step would die with no report and the deadline would have bought nothing.

NOT CLAIMED: nothing here runs msiexec, and no Windows machine was involved. What is tested is the decision -- what an invocation means -- which is the same division the rest of this harness keeps between residue.mjs deciding and msiexec measuring.

review.title: desktop-shell-ci.yml is the one workflow with no timeout at all
review.acceptance:
FOUND BY PL-0736, OUTSIDE ITS SURFACE. That task's acceptance names `ci.yml` and `windows.yml` and its allowedPaths hold exactly those two, so this file was not touched -- but the audit that produced the bounds read every workflow, and `windows-shell` is now the only job in this repository with no `timeout-minutes`, job-level or step-level.

Its shape is the one most likely to stall: `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, a Swatinem cache restore, and `cargo test`/`clippy`/`build --release` on a Windows runner, all of which reach the network and the first of which is the single slowest minute this repository spends.

REQUIRED: a job bound derived from an observed duration, with the derivation written beside it, in the same form `ci.yml` now uses.

REQUIRED: generous. A Windows Rust release build on a cold cache is genuinely long, and a bound that fires on one teaches people to re-run rather than to read.

OUT OF SCOPE: anything the job does, and the new `experiment-1a.yml`, which was written with `timeout-minutes: 45` already on it.
review.notes: P3 because this job is not on the release path -- `windows.yml` is what produces installers -- and because a six-hour stall here is visible as an unfinished run rather than as a wrong answer. Recorded now so it is written down rather than remembered.

review.title: Experiment 1a FAILED on real hardware and D1 still reads as if it had not been tested
review.acceptance:
THE RESULT, FROM THREE REAL-HARDWARE RUNS ON THE COMMANDER'S MACHINE. Run 1 (PL-0748's instrumentation) proved the harness could not explain itself. Run 2 (PL-0749's geometry fix) proved the child HWND was being resized to nothing. Run 3 (PL-0750's WebView2 transparency fallback) proved the remaining question: mpv initialises, the HEVC file opens, D3D11 comes up on an RTX 3050, d3d11va hardware decoding is active, the VO is gpu-next at 1280x720, the first video frame is reported shown, the Pause button reaches mpv, AND put_DefaultBackgroundColor(0,0,0,0) is accepted and reported successful. The commander still sees NO VIDEO -- only the WebView UI.

THE VERDICT, SCOPED TO EXACTLY WHAT WAS TESTED. The arrangement in section 1 -- a sibling child HWND at HWND_BOTTOM beneath a WINDOWED WebView2 controller, made transparent through put_DefaultBackgroundColor -- FAILS visible composition. Criterion 1 (hardware decode) PASS. Criterion 3 (click and control) PASS. Criterion 2 (compositing) FAIL. Criteria 4 through 7 UNOBSERVED, because they are behind criterion 2. Overall Experiment 1a NOT PASS.

REQUIRED: SECTION 1 STOPS READING AS IF THE ARRANGEMENT WERE PROVEN. It currently says 'This is not a theory' and cites Stremio shipping it. That citation is still true and must not be deleted -- what must be added is that OUR implementation of the same arrangement was tested on real hardware and did not composite, and that the difference between Stremio's result and ours is not yet explained. An unexplained difference from a shipping product is a finding, not a footnote.

REQUIRED: THE FAILURE IS RECORDED WITHOUT OVERSTATING ANYTHING ELSE. The run does not prove WebView2 cannot composite, does not prove Tauri is the wrong shell, does not prove DirectComposition will work, and does not prove Stremio's shipping arrangement is broken. It proves that THIS arrangement, as this harness built it, did not show video on one machine. Every sentence recorded must be defensible at that width.

REQUIRED: SECTION 10'S PASS CRITERIA ARE MARKED WITH WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, per criterion, rather than left as empty checkboxes that imply the experiment was never run. The matrix stays UNMET: one machine is not the matrix, and nothing here may be read as covering Windows 10 22H2, an Intel or AMD iGPU, a hybrid-graphics laptop, or a DPI transition.

REQUIRED: SECTION 11 (VERIFICATION STATUS) CARRIES THE RESULT. That section exists because the reviewer's standing complaint is documents claiming more than their evidence. A document whose section 1 rests on an experiment that has now failed, and whose verification status does not say so, is exactly that failure.

REQUIRED: SECTION 1 ALSO STOPS DESCRIBING --d3d11-output-mode=composition AS A DEFERRED V2 OPTIMISATION. review.title: Experiment 1c: can mpv composite beneath WebView2 in one DirectComposition visual tree
review.acceptance:
WHY THIS EXPERIMENT EXISTS. Experiment 1a's arrangement -- child HWND beneath a WINDOWED WebView2 controller -- failed visible composition on real hardware with mpv fully exonerated. PL-0751 records that. This is the replacement arrangement, and it is the one docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 1 already named and deferred.

THE ARRANGEMENT UNDER TEST. One host window. One DirectComposition device and target. One visual tree with two children: mpv's composition swapchain below, WebView2's composition visual above. Neither layer owns a window of its own, so neither can occlude the other by window z-order -- DWM composites them, with real per-pixel alpha.

THE THREE FACTS THAT MAKE IT BUILDABLE, each read from source rather than assumed, and each recorded in the build gate evidence with its file and line:
  1. mpv: --d3d11-output-mode=composition creates a D3D11 swapchain with NO window (d3d11_swapchain_opts.window is NULL), --d3d11-composition-size=WxH supplies the size a window would have, and the property display-swapchain returns the IDXGISwapChain pointer as an int64. VERIFIED PRESENT AT THE EXACT PINNED mpv COMMIT c152964208, so the pin and its digest do NOT move.
  2. WebView2: ICoreWebView2Environment3::CreateCoreWebView2CompositionController and ICoreWebView2CompositionController::SetRootVisualTarget / SendMouseInput / SendPointerInput / add_CursorChanged are all present in the already-locked webview2-com-sys 0.39.1, and webview2-com 0.39.1 ships the completion-handler wrappers, so no hand-written COM vtables.
  3. DirectComposition: DCompositionCreateDevice, IDCompositionDevice::CreateTargetForHwnd / CreateVisual / Commit, IDCompositionTarget::SetRoot and IDCompositionVisual::SetContent / AddVisual are all present in the already-locked windows 0.62.2 behind feature Win32_Graphics_DirectComposition.

REQUIRED: A MINIMAL RUST WINDOWS HOST, NOT THE TAURI SHELL, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL. Composition hosting is a CREATION-TIME decision: the webview must be created through CreateCoreWebView2CompositionController instead of CreateCoreWebView2Controller. wry and Tauri always create a windowed controller and hand it out afterwards through with_webview; there is no post-hoc conversion. That is why tauri-apps/wry PR 1762 is a change INSIDE wry rather than something an application can add. Forking wry for a throwaway experiment is not proportionate, so the experiment owns its window. The Liberty application is NOT rewritten and NOT touched.

REQUIRED: tauri-apps/wry PR 1762 IS TREATED AS REFERENCE, NOT AS A DEPENDENCY. It is a fork of wry 0.55.1, is not verified by CI by its own account, and its touch, pen and OLE drag-drop paths are explicitly best-effort or untested. What it is good for is the input-forwarding map, which it got right against production use: a host subclass forwards WM_MOUSE* to SendMouseInput with ScreenToClient conversion for wheel coordinates, calls MoveFocus(PROGRAMMATIC) on mouse-down and WM_SETFOCUS rather than forwarding keystrokes, forwards WM_POINTER* for touch and pen, applies the cached HCURSOR on WM_SETCURSOR, and calls SetBounds on WM_SIZE and NotifyParentWindowPositionChanged on WM_MOVE. Nothing is vendored, so no licence obligation is incurred; the knowledge is cited.

REQUIRED: THE EIGHT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA THE COMMANDER SET ARE EACH OBSERVABLE, and the harness says which it can and cannot answer by itself: (1) video visibly playing under the HTML overlay; (2) real transparency -- the HTML gradient TINTS the video rather than hiding it; (3) clickable HTML controls that pause and resume; (4) active GPU hardware decoding; (5) correct resize and window move; (6) correct DPI behaviour; (7) live telemetry including time-pos and avsync; (8) no orphaned processes and an acceptable shutdown.

REQUIRED: A DIAGNOSTIC LOG BESIDE THE EXE, on the PL-0748 pattern, which is the single highest-value thing three rounds of Experiment 1a taught. It must record each construction step and its outcome by name -- DComp device created, target created, both visuals created and attached, composition swapchain pointer obtained from display-swapchain, SetContent accepted, SetRootVisualTarget accepted -- so that a run which shows nothing says WHERE it stopped instead of requiring another round to find out. mpv's own log is captured as before.

REQUIRED: A FAILURE OF ANY CONSTRUCTION STEP IS REPORTED, NOT PAPERED OVER. If display-swapchain is unavailable, if the swapchain pointer is zero, if the WebView2 runtime is too old for the composition controller, or if DCompositionCreateDevice fails, each must produce its own line that names the step and says plainly that the experiment cannot be judged on that run.

REQUIRED: WINDOWS CI COMPILES IT AND PUBLISHES A REPRODUCIBLE ARTIFACT, on the experiment-1a.yml pattern: the same pinned-and-digest-gated mpv dev package, the same import library built from dumpbin /EXPORTS with its symbol floor and mpv_create assertion, the same PROVENANCE.txt binding artifact to commit and run, the same timeout. An override without a digest is refused, exactly as before.

MUST NOT: modify production playback, the PlayerAdapter boundary, apps/desktop, or anything outside this experiment's own directory and its own workflow. This is a throwaway.

MUST NOT: ship the experiment's GPL development libmpv binary inside the production installer, or be read as authorising any codec distribution. Section 9 and docs/LICENSING.md section 6 are unchanged.

MUST NOT: claim Experiment 1c PASSED. A green CI build proves the host compiles and links. Every one of the eight criteria is something a person has to look at on real hardware, and the OS/GPU/DPI matrix in section 10 is unchanged and unmet.

MUST NOT: change decision D1. That referral is PL-0751's and the decision is gpt-architect's.
review.notes: FILED 2026-10-10. Declares allowedPaths as experiments/exp-1c/** rather than experiments/** deliberately: that is the real write surface, and the broad declaration on PL-0748/0749/0750 is why three finished tasks are parked behind each other on one path. Reconnaissance for this task read mpv's d3d11 context and w32_common at the pinned commit, webview2-com-sys 0.39.1's bindings, windows 0.62.2's DirectComposition module, and wry PR 1762 -- before any code was written, because that order is what produced the last two correct diagnoses.

build.evidence:
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -D warnings: clean for BOTH x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and the host. cargo fmt --check: clean. repo:validate passed. Cargo.lock UNCHANGED -- no new dependency, no version moved.

THIS GATE REPLACES THE ONE RECORDED AGAINST 2af8855, WHICH WAS A GATE ON CODE WITH A CONFIRMED DEFECT. The previous evidence said "the harness compiles for Windows and the API surface it targets exists", and that was true. It was not sufficient: the code it passed put the video visual ABOVE the web visual, contradicting this task's own stated requirement. The task was returned to IN_PROGRESS with `start` rather than by fabricating a reviewer verdict, and this is the re-record.

THE DEFECT, PROVEN AGAINST MICROSOFT'S DOCUMENTATION RATHER THAN GUESSED. IDCompositionVisual::AddVisual's Remarks: "If the referenceVisual parameter is NULL, the specified visual is rendered above or below all children of the parent visual, depending on the value of the insertAbove parameter. If insertAbove is TRUE, the new child visual is above no sibling, therefore it is rendered BELOW all of its siblings. Conversely, if insertAbove is FALSE, the visual is below no sibling, therefore it is rendered ABOVE all of its siblings." With a NULL reference the flag is INVERTED relative to its own name. The delivered code called AddVisual(video, false, None) -- video rendered above all siblings -- and AddVisual(web, true, None) -- web rendered below all siblings. An opaque full-window video swapchain on top of the webview, which is precisely the commander's observation: video visible and playing, no HTML whatsoever. The source comment above those two lines asserted the opposite semantics and was written without reading the documentation, inside a comment that called this "the one thing this experiment must get right".

THE CORRECTION, IN A FORM THAT CANNOT FAIL THE SAME WAY. Video: AddVisual(video, true, None), which the quoted Remarks define as "rendered below all of its siblings". Web: AddVisual(web, true, Some(&video)) -- the EXPLICIT reference form, where the parameter means what its name says, "TRUE to place the new child visual in front of the visual specified by the referenceVisual parameter", and there is no counterintuitive NULL case left to misread. The quotation is in the source above the call so the next reader does not have to find it.

TWO FURTHER OMISSIONS, EACH A DOCUMENTED REQUIREMENT THE HARNESS WAS NOT MEETING, AND EACH CAPABLE OF PRODUCING THE SAME SYMPTOM ALONE:
  1. NO Commit AFTER SetRootVisualTarget. Microsoft's RootVisualTarget reference: "The app needs to commit on its device setting the RootVisualTarget property", and their sample calls Commit immediately after. The harness committed only when mpv's swapchain arrived -- roughly a second later, and never at all if it did not arrive -- which would have left the webview unattached for a reason no log line named. Tree::commit_named now commits there and logs it.
  2. SetIsVisible WAS NEVER CALLED. Zero occurrences of IsVisible in the previous source. ICoreWebView2Controller's reference says "If IsVisible is set to FALSE, the WebView2 is transparent and is not rendered" and documents NO DEFAULT for a composition-hosted controller; I could not establish one from Microsoft's pages. So the harness now READS IsVisible and logs the value found BEFORE setting it -- which settles empirically on the commander's machine what the documentation does not state -- and then sets it true regardless.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THIS ONE ROUND INSTEAD OF TWO. NavigateToString returning Ok means the navigation was QUEUED, the same distinction Experiment 1a lost a round to with loadfile. Four causes -- never navigated, navigated but the script never ran, rendered into a zero-area viewport, rendered but invisible -- produced one symptom and nothing could separate them. Added: add_NavigationCompleted reporting IsSuccess and, on failure, the WebErrorStatus number; add_DOMContentLoaded via ICoreWebView2_2, with a runtime too old to offer it reported rather than propagated as an error; and the page's own script posting a page-alive message carrying innerWidth, innerHeight, devicePixelRatio and the panel's measured offsetHeight. A 0x0 viewport now looks nothing like a z-order fault. Both handlers are installed BEFORE navigate(), so the first navigation cannot complete unobserved.

THE VIDEO RENDERER IS UNTOUCHED, as instructed. Same mpv property set, same --d3d11-output-mode=composition, same --d3d11-composition-size, same display-swapchain polling, same borrowed-not-adopted SetContent, same attach logic, same resize path. The part of the run that worked was not edited.

ALL THREE CHANGED MODULES ARE REALLY COMPILED FOR WINDOWS, proved rather than assumed: deliberate type errors inserted simultaneously into dcomp.rs (a string as AddVisual's referenceVisual), web.rs (a string to SetIsVisible) and host.rs (an i32 to on_load) produced exactly 3 errors, naming src/dcomp.rs:149, src/web.rs:271 and src/host.rs:159. All reverted.

NO NEW DEPENDENCY. add_NavigationCompleted, add_DOMContentLoaded, NavigationCompletedEventArgs::IsSuccess/WebErrorStatus, ICoreWebView2_2, ICoreWebView2Controller::IsVisible/SetIsVisible and webview2-com's NavigationCompletedEventHandler/DOMContentLoadedEventHandler wrappers were all already in the locked webview2-com-sys 0.39.1 and webview2-com 0.39.1. The lockfile is byte-identical.

NOT CLAIMED: that the overlay now appears. NOTHING HERE HAS RUN. What the commander's run established is that the video path works end to end on real hardware -- video visible and moving, hardware decode on an RTX 3050, DComp tree built, swapchain attached, composition controller initialised -- and that is kept. Whether the two layers composite with real alpha is what the next run decides, and there are now THREE possible outcomes rather than two: both layers visible and the gradient tinting (the pass); HTML visible with no video (a NEW failure, meaning composition hosting ignores DefaultBackgroundColor rather than that the layering is wrong); or still no HTML (the z-order was not the only cause, and the four new log lines say which stage stopped). Experiment 1c is NOT PASS, Experiment 1a remains FAIL, PW-0103 is untouched and decision D1 is unchanged and with gpt-architect under PL-0751.

recommended.title: The distribution inventory runs nowhere until the Windows workflow calls it
recommended.acceptance:
REQUIRED: the Windows package job runs scripts/windows/distribution-inventory.mjs against the PACKAGE BUILD OUTPUT after the bundle is produced, and against the INSTALLED TREE inside the lifecycle run, with each invocation naming which tree it is reporting on. Two trees, two reports, never conflated.

REQUIRED: it runs even when a later step fails, for the same reason the installer-log upload does -- the inventory of a build is most interesting on the run that went wrong.

REQUIRED: its unit suite joins npm run test:scripts, and therefore gains a step in the CI validate job, because PL-0714's mirror-check fails a build whose alias names a suite with no step. A script nothing runs is this repository's most-repeated defect and PL-0737 must not become the sixth instance.

OUT OF SCOPE: what the inventory says. This task makes it run and makes its output readable.
recommended.notes:
FILED ROUND 113 alongside PL-0737, which it exists to wire in. BLOCKED BY SURFACE, not by work: .github/workflows/windows.yml is reserved by PL-0733 and package.json by PL-0728, both in gpt-architect's review queue. Same shape as PL-0736 and recorded the same way rather than worked around.

SURFACE CORRECTED 2026-10-05, BEFORE THE NEXT CLAIM RATHER THAN DURING IT. The task could not satisfy its own third clause. That clause requires the inventory's unit suite to join `npm run test:scripts` and therefore to gain a step in the CI validate job -- because PL-0714's mirror-check fails a build whose alias names a suite with no step -- and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was not among allowedPaths. Whoever claimed it would have reached that clause, found the file outside the surface, and either widened it mid-implementation or quietly skipped the clause. Both are worse than fixing the declaration while nobody owns the task.

ADDING ci.yml MEANS THIS TASK NOW OVERLAPS PL-0736 UNTIL THAT ONE CLEARS REVIEW, and that is the correct state rather than an obstacle: `ai:claim` will refuse, which is the control plane saying the two cannot safely be held at once. It was already refusing on windows.yml alone.

recommended.title: test:scripts and the CI validate job can disagree in one direction without anything noticing
recommended.acceptance:
FILED ON A FALSE PREMISE AND REWRITTEN BEFORE ANY WORK. The original said apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs "is run by nothing" and called it the fifth instance of a suite no gate asks. IT RUNS IN CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml, validate job, step id `notices-suite`, `node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs`, added by PL-0714. The claim came from reading that file's own header comment -- "NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY RUNS THIS FILE AUTOMATICALLY YET" -- which was true when PW-0208 wrote it and was made false by PL-0714 a round later. The correction is recorded as a defect.found event.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND IT IS SMALLER AND MORE INTERESTING.

1. THE SUITE IS NOT IN `npm run test:scripts`, so it is not in `npm run check` either. It runs on every push and never on a developer's machine through the command this repository tells people to run. That is a coverage asymmetry, not an absence.

2. PL-0714's `mirror-check` CANNOT DETECT THAT, and this is the finding worth the task. It derives the alias's scripts from package.json, derives the job's from the workflow, and fails when a script in the ALIAS has no STEP. The reverse -- a step with no alias entry -- is not checked in either direction. Measured: adding notices.test.mjs to the alias makes the check report "every suite in the alias has a step in this job" and exit 0, and removing it again also exits 0. The mechanism PL-0714 built to end a hand-kept list is itself one-directional, so half the drift it was built for is still invisible.

REQUIRED: `npm run test:scripts` names the suite, so `npm run check` covers it locally.
REQUIRED: the mirror check becomes BIDIRECTIONAL -- a suite step in the validate job with no entry in the alias fails too, with the same kind of message. PL-0714's own words apply: "the note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step did not keep it in step on any of the three occasions", and a one-directional check is half a note.
REQUIRED: both directions are proven to FAIL, by removing an entry from each side in turn and showing the check goes red, not merely by showing it green today.
REQUIRED: the stale header comment in notices.test.mjs is corrected, because it is what produced the false premise above. A comment that outlives the code it describes is the failure this project keeps recording.

OUT OF SCOPE: making apps/desktop an npm workspace. Round 106 measured that and it breaks repo:validate; the account is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.
recommended.notes:
FILED ROUND 111 by claude-infra during PW-0208, ON A FALSE PREMISE, and rewritten the same round by claude-lead after checking the workflow rather than trusting a comment. Surface widened from package.json alone to include ci.yml (the mirror check lives there) and notices.test.mjs (its header carries the stale claim). Priority dropped P2 -> P3: a local-coverage gap and a one-directional check, not a suite running nowhere.

COLLIDES WITH: .github/workflows/ci.yml is PL-0717's (REVIEW) and PL-0726's (REVIEW) surface, so this cannot be active beside either. That is why it is not being executed now.
